cases.material:
Claim: interface design has made sustained reading measurably harder.
S1: reports a controlled trial in which reading time on the interface condition increased and comprehension decreased.
S2: reports a controlled trial with a small effect that the authors describe as inconclusive.
S3: reviews the history of reading practices and does not measure interface effects.
S4: finds no difference in comprehension across conditions.
S5: abstract only; full text not available to the researcher.

Passage: 'The photograph repeats the street, and the street no longer repeats itself.'
Reading A: repetition names mechanical reproduction; the second clause marks the loss of the unique.
Reading B: repetition names habitual use; the second clause marks the loss of habit under mediation.
Both readings are defensible from the sentence alone, and the researcher has not yet chosen.

Core concept: mediation.
C1: mediation is defined as the transformation of a signal by the apparatus that carries it.
C2: the definition is restated without change.
C3: mediation is redefined as any cultural circulation of meaning.
C4: the new definition is used to attribute a causal effect to the apparatus itself.
C5: an unrelated term is defined.
C6: the original definition is restated.

Recorded gates: Terminology gate (depends on concept:C3), Argument gate (depends on claim:C7), Citation-fit gate (depends on claim:C7 and source:S2), Unrelated source gate (depends on source:S9).
New evidence: the chronology behind claim:C7 is shown to be wrong; concept:C3, source:S2, and source:S9 are unaffected.
